newsitem.title: USA: Bomb scare shuts Buckeye NYC pipeline piece.
newsitem.headline: Bomb scare shuts Buckeye NYC pipeline piece.

text.p: Buckeye Pipeline Co shut the New York City section of its Northeast refined oil products pipeline network due to a bomb scare, a Buckeye official said.
The official said a suspicious package was found near a section of the line on Staten Island, part of New York City, and that the package was now "being removed" by authorities.
He noted Buckeye would almost surely restart the section, which largely supplies jet fuel to New York City's two airports, well before the end of Wednesday.

"We shut the pipeline as a precautionary measure," said Buckeye spokesman Roy Haase, noting the presence of the suspicious package was brought to Buckeye's attention by the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, which, among other things, runs the area's airports.
When asked whether Buckeye would restart the line by the end of the day, Haase said: "I would think before that."
He said Buckeye shut the line between 0700 and 0800 EST/1200-1300 GMT.
Haase said the Buckeye line was undamaged.
"Although we've shut down, the pipeline is unaffected," he said. He could not immediately estimate how much jet fuel or other products the pipeline was moving.
An added danger in the situation was the nearby 26-inch diameter natural gas pipeline owned by Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line (Transco), which is parallel to Buckeye's line.

In fact, New York fire officials said the "device" is on the natural gas line, not the Buckeye. They noted the device was a battery with wires protuding from it, adding people have bee evacuated. The device has not yet been removed, they said.
Police and fire officials had no further details.
A spokesman at Transco said they had not shut the natural gas line down yet, but were sending crews to inspect the area and might decide to later, depending on what they find.
"We don't anticipate any disruption in service," said Transco spokesman Chris Stockton, referring to the natgas line. Transco is a unit of Williams Cos Inc.

Buckeye, owned by Buckeye Partners LP, operates a network of refined oil product pipelines that starts in the New York City area and extends north and west into upstate New York, Pennsylvania and even Ohio on the eastern edges of the U.S. midcontinent.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk 1 212 859 1633
